item.title: AB de Villiers weighs in on Sandpapergate and claims Australia ball tampered in first test of 2018 series
item.description: Former South Africa captain AB de Villiers has ramped up the ongoing drama of sandpapergate, alleging Australia were ball tampering from the first Test of the 2018 series in Durban. The scandal initially centred around the third Test in Cape Town, where Cameron Bancroft was caught red-handed by television cameras using sandpaper to generate reverse swing. The drama reopened after more than eight years with the publication of Usman Khawaja ’s autobiography, which included a variety of new admissions, including that the same practice had been taking place in the second at Gqeberha, then known as Port Elizabeth. Bancroft and David Warner , who received lengthy bans for their roles alongside Steve Smith , corroborated Khawaja’s account. Meanwhile, a number of senior figures, including current Australia captain Pat Cummins and the former head coach Darren Lehmann , have issued fresh denials surrounding their own knowledge of the plot. Now De Villiers, who was a key part of the Proteas side in the ill-tempered series, has raised the stakes with new claims about the Durban game – Australia’s only win of the tour. Speaking on his own YouTube channel, ABD360, he said: “It’s become really personal for all the people involved and I do have sympathy for them. Obviously not sympathy for what took place on that day and who knows how many games before then. “I see everyone is sort of admitting that in Port Elizabeth it also happened. I can very much tell you Durban was no different, in the first Test. Go look at the footage. Absolutely no doubt in my mind. “It started in Durban, by the way, not in PE. I’m very happy for people to quote me on that. Australia captain Pat Cummins denied the allegations during a lengthy press conference in Sydney (Reuters) “We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time. Way too early for anyone to reverse a ball at Kingsmead. Trust me, I’ve played a lot of cricket there. “So whatever they did there, whether it was sandpaper or (a) nail, I don’t care. The fact of the matter is they were caught and everyone knew. Just stand up as say ‘we were wrong’. A lot is at stake now because they lied.” Cummins has repeatedly distanced himself from the tampering allegations, rejecting any role in the events during a long press conference in Sydney. He has since received the unanimous backing of the Cricket Australia board to continue as captain following growing speculation over his future. Khawaja and Warner, on the other hand, have been stood down from commentary duties on Fox Cricket for the ongoing England T20 series. “I just feel they should have stuck together as a unit. They threw the guys under the bus and forced a situation like this to pop up again eight years later,” concluded De Villiers.

item.title: Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy: Shivam Dube, Angkrish Raghuvanshi star as Mumbai thrash Chhattisgarh
item.description: India allrounder Shivam Dube claimed three for 21, while Angkrish Raghuvanshi struck an unbeaten 84 (63b, 8x4, 3x6) as Mumbai thrashed Chhattisgarh by nine wickets in a Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Elite Group D match at Eden Gardens in Kolkata on Saturday. After bowling out Chhattisgarh for 159 in 18.2 overs, Mumbai chased down the target in 18.5 overs, finishing at 162 for one. Raghuvanshi, who had managed scores of 27, 4 and 0 in his first three outings, bounced back with his career-best T20 score. Hardik Tamore (42) and Musheer Khan (29 not out) provided useful support. Brief scores: Chhattisgarh 159 (Vikalp Tiwari 41; Shivam Dube 3-21) lost to Mumbai 162/1 in 18.5 overs (Angkrish Raghuvanshi 84 not out, Hardik Tamore 42) by nine wickets. Dahiya sets up Delhi victory Tejasvi Dahiya smashed 95 off just 36 balls, including six sixes and nine fours, while captain Priyansh Arya contributed 62 as Delhi piled up 232 for six against Haryana in Indore. Haryana managed 189 for eight in reply, handing Delhi a 43-run victory. Suyash Sharma claimed three for 31. Brief scores: Delhi 232/6 (Tejasvi Dahiya 95, Priyansh Arya 62; Anuj Thakral 3-35, Sumit Kumar 3-52) beat Haryana 189/8 (Samant Jakhar 33, Sumit Kumar 33, Ankit Kumar 32; Suyash Sharma 3-31) by 43 runs. Juyal, Bhuvneshwar shine Aryan Juyal’s 83 (55b, 10x4, 2x6) and Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s three-wicket haul powered Uttar Pradesh to a 12-run win over defending champions Jharkhand at the Wankhede Stadium. UP were struggling at 33 for four in the sixth over before Juyal and Sameer Rizvi (39 off 26 balls) added 96 for the fifth wicket. Shivam Mavi’s unbeaten 19 off eight balls lifted UP to 181 for seven. Jharkhand managed 169 for eight despite half-centuries from Utkarsh Singh (58) and Md Kounain Quraishi (52). Bhuvneshwar finished with three for 39, while Yash Dayal claimed two for 29. Playing his first SMAT match after returning from New Zealand, Kuldeep Yadav went wicketless, conceding 37 runs in four overs. Brief scores:UP 181/7 (Aryan Juyal 83, Sameer Rizvi 39; Harsh Raj 3-34) beat Jharkhand 169/8 (Utkarsh Singh 58, Md Kounain Quraishi 52; Bhuvneshwar Kumar 3-39) by 12 runs. Chandigarh stun Karnataka Chandigarh bundled out Karnataka for just 95 before cruising to a seven-wicket win at the MCA ground in BKC. Brief scores: Karnataka 95 in 17.5 overs (Karun Nair 25; Hardik Chowdhry 3-17, Bhagmender Lather 3-19) lost to Chandigarh 96/3 in 13.5 overs (Shivam Bhambri 52 not out) by seven wickets. item.title: College basketball roundup: Stanford women match worst start since 2017, fall to Portland
item.description: Stanford women's basketball head coach Kate Paye reacts during the first half of the Cardinal's loss against the Washington Huskies on Friday at Alaska Airlines Arena in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) The Stanford women's basketball team is off to its worst start since 2017 after falling to host Portland 73-62 on Sunday night. The Cardinal (4-3) were outscored by eight in the fourth quarter and the Pilots (4-2) totaled 33 points off turnovers. Point guard Hailee Swain, who entered averaging 20.5 points per game, was held to 10 on 4-for-14 shooting (0-for-5 from 3-point). Inés Sotelo Míguez scored a team-high 18 Sara Mangan led Portland with 18 points off the bench. The last time these teams met, Stanford squandered a 13-point second-half lead to end its 2024-25 season in a 69-68 overtime defeat in the first round of the WBIT. The 2017-18 Cardinal suffered losses to No. 5 Ohio State, No. 1 Connecticut and again against the Buckeyes (then ranked ninth) in their first seven games, only to finish second in the Pac-12 and advance to the Sweet Sixteen. These 2026-27 Cardinal suffered losses to unranked Arizona and Portland sandwiched around a program-worst 55-point defeat to No. 16 Washington. USF 81, Cal State-Bakersfield 58: The Dons built a 20-point halftime lead and breezed to the victory at home. Candy Edokpaigbe led USF (5-1) with 18 points and Aina Cargol and Lucia Yenes added 15 apiece. The Dons shot 50.9% from the field and 11-for-24 from 3-point range. Dresha Moore led Bakersfield (1-3) with 18 points. Men St. Mary's 94, Menlo 78: The Gaels had to overcome a surprisingly strong first half from the Division II Oaks from Atherton, leading just 43-41 at the half. But behind an overpowering effort on the boards (outrebounding Menlo 39-23) and led by a 20-point night from Lithuanian sophomore guard Mantas Juzenar, St. Mary's pulled away in the second half to improve to 6-1 on the season. item.title: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak shrugs off Denver return following Broncos loss
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Raiders’ Klint Kubiak shrugs off Denver return following Broncos loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Going home feels great until you leave with a 38-24 loss. Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak had zero interest in reminiscing after his Denver Broncos homecoming ended in defeat on Nov. 22. Kubiak grew up in the Denver area, spent four seasons across two stints on the Broncos’ coaching staff and watched his father, Gary Kubiak, win a Super Bowl as Denver’s head coach. Still, when reporters asked about returning to Empower Field at Mile High, Kubiak shut down the nostalgia immediately. “Yeah, I could. I don’t want to,” Kubiak said. “I wanted to win this game today. And we didn’t win. So we gotta go win next week.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Las Vegas fell to 4-7 after digging an early 17-0 hole. Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza sparked a comeback before halftime, hitting running back Ashton Jeanty for a 68-yard touchdown in the second quarter before finding tight end Ian Thomas for a 19-yard score in the third to tie the game at 17. Mendoza finished 18-of-37 for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception while playing without injured star tight end Brock Bowers. Jeanty carried the offense with 79 rushing yards on 11 attempts and 90 receiving yards on five catches. Denver’s pass rush also sacked Mendoza five times, and nine Las Vegas penalties for 63 yards stalled momentum. Denver improved to 8-2 behind rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who pounded out 111 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries. Quarterback Bo Nix added 225 passing yards and a score. Wide receiver Jack Bech caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Mendoza with 4:29 left to pull the Raiders within 31-24, but cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian sealed the win with a 35-yard pick-six just after coming out of the two-minute warning. Kubiak expressed optimism that Bowers can return from ankle and quadriceps injuries when Las Vegas visits the Cleveland Browns next Sunday night. Kubiak gets another shot at the Broncos on Dec. 20 in Las Vegas. Until then, sentimental storylines remain off limits. item.title: 'We failed the exam!' - Cristian Chivu fumes as 'soft and shallow' Inter throw away two-goal leads three times in chaotic Atalanta draw
item.description: FBL-ITA-SERIEA-ATALANTA-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter head coach Cristian Chivu has delivered a stinging assessment of his side's mental fragility after they squandered multiple leads in a breathtaking 4-4 draw against Atalanta. The Nerazzurri boss claimed his players "failed the exam" during a chaotic evening in Bergamo that saw them surrender a two-goal cushion on three separate occasions. Late collapse ruins Pio Esposito's hat-trick Atalanta snatched a dramatic point in Bergamo through Charles De Ketelaere’s second goal and a stoppage-time penalty from Franck, cancelling out Petar Sucic’s spot-kick that had made it 4-2. That late collapse ruined a landmark evening for Pio Esposito , who followed up his strong Nations League displays for Italy by netting his first Serie A hat-trick. Inter’s frustration was compounded by two penalty calls. The visitors felt Davide Zappacosta deserved a red card rather than a booking for a goal-line elbow clearance, before Alessandro Bastoni conceded the decisive late spot-kick for an unintentional handball with his arms raised above his shoulder. Chivu slams 'soft and shallow' Nerazzurri display Speaking to DAZN Italia , Chivu lambasted his side's lack of edge. "We were leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, so this is the regret," Chivu said after the game. "We had an idea of what we should’ve done and did not do, we should’ve controlled the advantage, then when we felt them snapping at our heels, we immediately restored the two-goal cushion. "I think we failed the exam in the final minutes. It’s hard to say why we were unable to control the lead. We have to congratulate Atalanta, as they sensed that we were a bit shallow, and pumped crosses into the box, put bodies in there, while we were a little soft compared to our usual approach. "I’m sorry, I see this as two gifted points, but we will learn from it and know now to let the intensity and mentality drop in the next games." He also pinpointed lapses at set-pieces and inside the box. "The second Atalanta goal came from a corner, identical to one where Pepo had just made a great save moments earlier, so we did not learn from it," Chivu continued. "When we got to 4-2, our defence was then static in a chaotic situation. We need a certain determination and focus in these situations, and we were negligent in that area today." Chivu altered his wide setup late on, though he insisted mentality mattered most. "I felt we were suffering on the wings, partly because we were too soft, we were allowing the space to put the crosses in too easily. First, it were Spurs winning at the Bridge for just the second time since 1990. Now, it’s Leeds United walking away with all three points for the first time since 1999. And they probably were partying like it, too. And it’s not like either of those two results were undeserved. There were no miracles here. We weren’t undone by an unlucky bounce or an egregious call, even if the penalty called on Morgan Rogers was a bit harsh (if the shoulder or shirt sleeve count for offside, it shouldn’t be a handball). item.title: 'You don't win 345 matches just by defending' - Diego Simeone hits back at critics after breaking Luis Aragones' all-time La Liga record
item.description: FBL-ESP-LIGA-ATLETICO-BARCELONA - AFP Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has hit back at critics who label his side overly defensive after breaking Luis Aragones' all-time La Liga wins record on Sunday. The Argentine secured his 345th Spanish top-flight victory with a comfortable 3-0 triumph at Getafe, moving past the late club legend's long-standing benchmark of 344 wins. Argentine coach surpasses club legend Simeone claimed his 345th La Liga victory in just his 567th match , needing 189 fewer games than Aragones took to reach 344 before his final win in 2004. Goals from Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso put Atletico in control by half-time, both assisted by Julian Alvarez . Alejandro Grimaldo added a late penalty after Djene Dakonam was sent off following a VAR review for fouling Alexander Sorloth. Simeone rejects defensive football label Reflecting on the milestone after the match, Simeone admitted the achievement meant a great deal: "It makes me happy. I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this." Despite evolving Atletico's style considerably since arriving in 2011, the coach still faces familiar jibes about his tactics. Addressing the scrutiny on Spanish television channel Movistar , he added: "Then there's the constant criticism we face. I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it. "This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?" Longevity defines remarkable Atletico reign Taking over a struggling club almost 15 years ago, Simeone has transformed Atletico into Spanish football's established third force, disrupting Real Madrid and Barcelona while lifting eight trophies. Although rival coaches may hold higher win percentages or larger trophy hauls, few can match his resilience and consistency at the top level. Even the deepest scars of his tenure, two Champions League final defeats to Real, one on penalties and another in extra time after a stoppage-time equaliser, failed to derail him. Instead, the black-clad tactician has maintained the same touchline intensity, passing the all-time record from one Atletico great to another 22 years after Aragones set it. Atletico chase La Liga title leaders Sunday's result made it eight wins in nine league games, lifting Atletico to 31 points , just two behind Real and five adrift of leaders Barcelona. With Baena, Alvarez and Cardoso clicking, Simeone's side have built real momentum heading into the winter schedule. Sustaining this attacking sharpness will be vital if they are to turn another strong run into a genuine title charge.

item.title: ‘Listen to me’: What John Harbaugh ran up to Liam Coen and said after Giants beat Jaguars
item.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images The New York Giants picked up a statement 23-18 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife Stadium. Both teams came into the game with a lot of confidence, but not many people would’ve put their money on the Giants getting the job done. That’s how good the Jaguars have been this season, which is probably why their coach, Liam Coen, earned some praise from John Harbaugh after the game. John Harbaugh praises Liam Coen after Giants beat Jaguars The game between the New York Giants and the Jacksonville Jaguars was a great watch. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson’s unit intercepted MVP candidate Trevor Lawrence twice and generated constant pressure. That led to Jacksonville converting just one of six red-zone trips and settling for two field goals early, four overall. There was some controversy in the end, with a refereeing decision going against the Jaguars, but their head coach Coen still gracefully shook Harbaugh’s hand. Cameras saw that exchange, where Harbaugh was seen running up to Coen, shaking his hand, pulling him closer and offering him and his side some big praise. The Athletic’s Ian O’Connor transcribed the Giants coach’s words on X : “Hey, listen to me. You got a hell of a team. And you have done a great job with this football team. You are a very well-coached football team.” Harbaugh is one of the best coaches in the NFL, and he has seen it all in the game over the last few decades. He knows what it takes to build a championship-winning side. That is why the 64-year-old’s praise for Coen should mean so much to the Jaguars coach, who is still very young in his coaching career. Despite the defeat, Jacksonville are still 7-3 for the season and remain on top of the AFC South standings. It remains to be seen how they will bounce back when they face the Titans next week. (INA FASSBENDER) Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovac backed struggling winger Ethan Nwaneri to find form ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash at parent club Arsenal. Nwaneri, 19, joined Dortmund on a season-long loan from the Gunners on deadline day, but has not been a beneficiary of the German club's impressive start to the campaign. Unbeaten in Germany this season, Dortmund sit two points clear of defending champions Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga table. But Nwaneri has just one assist in 13 appearances and has gone from being a regular starter to occupying largely a bench role, with some media outlets reporting the loan spell could end early in January. Nwaneri burst onto the scene with Arsenal, becoming the youngest player in Premier League history when he made his debut aged 15 years and 181 days in September 2022. The teenager scored 10 goals and laid on two assists in 51 matches for the Gunners, but moved to French side Marseille last season chasing more game time. After scoring in his opening match, a 3-1 win over Lens in January, Nwaneri only netted once more during his time at the Ligue 1 club and was mostly relegated to the bench. Clearly a fan of a fast start, Nwaneri assisted a goal in his opening Dortmund match but has yet to register another goal or assist. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf received a fine for a Week 4 taunting penalty against the Cleveland Browns. Getty Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf is facing the prospect of NFL punishment for trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye during Sunday’s game, and the Philadelphia Eagles cornerback had a harsh take on the incident after the game. Metcalf was ejected from the game after his scuffle with DeJean, one of several incidents where the former Pro Bowl receiver lost his cool. The Steelers wide receiver is expected to face more NFL punishment for the incident. After the game, DeJean shared his thoughts on the incident. Cooper DeJean Calls Out DK Metcalf Speaking to reporters, DeJean said that Metcalf was growing frustrated with his shrinking role in the offense and took it out on his opponent. “He wasn’t getting the ball a whole lot during that game. Some receivers, they let that get to them,” DeJean said in a postgame video shared by ESPN’s Tim McManus . “Obviously he tried to take it out on me.” Metcalf had just one reception for 2 yards in the loss. The veteran receiver has 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns through 10 games this season. DeJean didn’t seem to take the incident personally, saying he and Metcalf were just competing hard against each other. “We were just competing,” DeJean said . “Things like that happen in football. It wasn’t anything crazy. No one was really saying anything, it was just two guys going at it. He was trying block me, I was trying to get him off of me, things like that. Obviously, it carries over to whatever that was when he got thrown out.” DK Metcalf Expected to Face NFL Suspension Metcalf left the stadium without talking to reporters after Sunday’s game, and could soon learn his fate from the NFL after it reviews the incident. item.title: Celtic Fans Should Love One Thing Martin O'Neill Did vs St Mirren
item.description: Celtic finally got themselves a one-sided win, 4-1 against St Mirren this weekend. While their lead atop the table remains the same, with Rangers also winning, it should act as a much-needed confidence booster for a team that has struggled to convince all season. There were some decisions that Martin O'Neill made on the day that should have been made a long time ago. And one of them surrounded the club's record signing, Kasper Hogh. Hogh was left on the bench as an unused substitute against St Mirren. Of course, one would have thought that this would have been a good chance to bring on the struggling striker. I, for one, do not agree with that viewpoint. Playing for Celtic should always be based on merit. And unfortunately, Hogh has not shown enough to convince that he deserves minutes ahead of anybody right now. Hogh has struggled badly in Celtic colours In 17 of his 18 outings for Celtic, Hogh has not found the back of the net. That would not have been the plan when they spent a club-record transfer fee on signing the striker. A lot more would have been expected of a striker who scored against teams like Atletico Madrid, Inter Milan and Manchester City in the Champions League last season. But he has looked lost away from Bodo/Glimt's system. Of course, there are those who point towards some positive moments with his hold-up play and link-up. That being said, that is a case of lowering the bar to meet the current circumstances rather than Hogh rising to meet expectations. Despite that, for a while, O'Neill tried to accommodate Hogh in the team. Often, he started him, at the expense of moving the in-form Camilo Duran out wide . In the game against St Mirren though, it looked like O'Neill might have finally given up on the Hogh experiment. The manager brought on Shim Mheuka, a loanee from Chelsea, ahead of the Danish international. Celtic Target Suffers Injury, Ruled Out for 6-8 Weeks The Celtic transfer target has suffered an injury and has been ruled out of action for 6-8 weeks. Did Mheuka deserve his chance ahead of Hogh? Mheuka has spent most of his time on the sidelines since arriving on loan from Chelsea, even though he has looked lively when on the pitch. Right now, Hogh is not offering much. So, if the selection is to be based on merit, Mheuka deserves a fair shake of things at the very least. So, fans should not have an issue with Mheuka getting opportunities for the time being. item.title: Tapia's Brace Puts Messi's Inter Miami on Brink of Elimination
item.description: Tapia's Brace Puts Messi's Inter Miami on Brink of Elimination Gonzalo Tapia scored twice as the seventh-seeded Columbus Crew stunned defending MLS Cup champion Inter Miami 3-0 at Nu Stadium on Saturday, taking a 1-0 lead in their best-of-three first-round series. Taha Habroune added the third goal, and Lionel Messi was held without a goal or assist for the night. Miami must now win Game 2 in Columbus on Friday to force a decisive Game 3 back in Florida on Dec. 2. A second loss ends the title defense in the opening round. How two mistakes turned the game The result turned on moments Miami created for itself. Goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair came off his line and brought down Tapia in the box in the eighth minute, and the Chilean forward converted the penalty himself. Twenty-eight minutes later, defender Gonzalo Luján picked up a second yellow card for a dangerous tackle, leaving Miami to play the final 54 minutes with ten men. Columbus used the extra space to control the second half. Habroune doubled the lead in the 52nd minute with what was described as a team move, and Tapia added his second six minutes later after turning Yannick Bright and running in alone on goal. Patrick Schulte made five saves at the other end, denying Messi on a point-blank effort and a free kick in the first half. Why Columbus arrived in form This was not a one-off. Columbus sat 15th in the Eastern Conference on Sept. 1 but entered the playoffs having won six straight regular-season matches, the longest active streak in the league. Interim coach Laurent Courtois even pulled Tapia with more than half an hour left to manage his fitness and avoid a second yellow card that would have ruled him out of Game 2 — a sign the Crew felt the result was already secure. Tapia himself is part of a broader scouting pipeline between MLS and Brazil's top flight. The Chilean forward joined Columbus in August on loan from São Paulo, where he had spent the previous year in Série A after arriving from River Plate. His scoring burst in Miami adds to a growing trend of MLS clubs pulling frontline talent directly out of Brazilian football rather than waiting for players to wash out of South America first. What a Game 2 loss would mean Miami also lost Luján's availability for Friday's game, and Messi picked up a yellow card late in the first half for throwing a ball into Tapia's face during a throw-in, an incident replays showed clearly but the referee did not act on beyond the booking. None of that changes the math: Inter Miami, the No. 2 seed and reigning champion, now needs a road win in Columbus simply to survive. A repeat of Saturday's pattern — an early set-piece concession, a card, and a Tapia finish — would end their season in the first round for the second time in three years.

item.title: Brothers Sam and Andy Houghton take on sidecarcross racing
item.description: For Sam and Andy Houghton, competitive sidecarcross is much more than a motorsport. It is a shared passion, a test of teamwork, and a powerful expression of brotherhood. The two brothers compete together in a demanding form of motocross where one rider controls the motorcycle while the other moves dynamically inside the attached sidecar to maintain balance and navigate challenging corners. Every race brings intense adrenaline, powerful acceleration, and split-second decisions. Unlike traditional motorcycle racing, sidecarcross requires both competitors to work almost as one person. Their movements must be perfectly coordinated because even a small difference in timing can affect the bike's direction, stability, and performance. Their journey into motorsport began when they were young. Sam started riding motorcycles at around four years old and began competitive racing when he was approximately ten. He quickly developed a passion for the sport, eventually winning his first championship with a local club at around eleven or twelve years of age. Over the following years, he progressed through different competitions and championships, building a promising racing career. However, in 2005, when he was 24, everything changed after a serious training accident. Sam went over the handlebars and landed heavily on his back, shattering his T7 vertebra and leaving him with a spinal cord injury that resulted in permanent mobility challenges. Following the accident, Sam spent considerable time in hospital and several years away from competitive racing. Although his circumstances had changed dramatically, his passion for motorcycles never disappeared. The desire to return to the track remained strong, and eventually, he and his brother discovered sidecarcross as a way to get back into competitive motorsport. Rather than allowing his injury to end his racing journey, Sam found a different way to pursue the activity he loved. One of the most interesting aspects of their partnership is the physical and technical responsibility each brother carries. Andy controls the motorcycle, while Sam works from the sidecar, constantly shifting his body weight from one side to another to help turn the machine and keep it balanced. There is no sitting comfortably during a race. The passenger must throw their weight across the sidecar, respond instantly to changing conditions, and anticipate the driver's movements. Both brothers need to understand each other's decisions without hesitation. Their relationship as siblings gives them an additional advantage because years of familiarity and trust help them develop an almost instinctive understanding of one another. For Sam, the greatest reward comes from the feeling of being on the track, leaning into corners, and experiencing the motorcycle drifting sideways at speed. The 21-year-old UAE all-rounder enters Season 5 with Dubai Capitals, who secured his services for $95,000 at the auction. Having spent four years in the competition with the Gulf Giants, Aayan believes the exposure to international stars has helped him improve, not just in franchise cricket but also at the international level, where he's played 48 ODIs and 40 T20Is. “I need to do well in this league. To do well, I need to learn so many things from these international players. They have been playing franchise leagues all around the world. His move to Dubai Capitals brings another opportunity to share a dressing room with established names such as Faf du Plessis, Marcus Stoinis, Phil Salt and Noor Ahmad. Having previously played alongside the likes of Andre Russell, Sunil Narine, Kieron Pollard and Nicholas Pooran, the UAE youngster says the initial nervousness of being around international stars has gradually given way to familiarity. “I was a bit nervous at the start, but now I know these international players. They are so good to be around. They know me, and we know each other,” he said. For the UAE and Associate players, however, the value of the ILT20 extends beyond exposure. The competition's playing conditions mandate at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one ICC Associate Member player in every playing XI, creating regular opportunities for regional talent to compete alongside international stars. Teams must also maintain a minimum of four UAE and four Afghanistan players in their squads, alongside representation from Ireland, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and another Associate nation. Aayan sees the UAE-player requirement as an opportunity rather than added pressure, with consistent performances potentially opening doors to other franchise leagues. “For us, two players to play in all the games is a big thing. item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images Cam Skattebo brought back his trademark backflip celebration after the New York Giants secured a 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars, despite recently promising to retire the move. The running back had decided to stop performing backflips after watching Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffer an ACL injury while celebrating a sack against the New England Patriots. However, Skattebo could not resist bringing it back after producing a crucial late run to help the Giants seal an impressive victory. Cam Skattebo explains why he brought back his backflip celebration Skattebo’s celebration came after he picked up a five-yard first down on the Giants’ final drive, allowing them to run down the clock and secure the win. After getting up, the second-year running back screamed, flexed and performed the very move he had recently claimed was retired. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reacted to the moment on X: “Backflip has come out of its brief retirement.” Giants head coach John Harbaugh also noticed his running back’s decision to break his promise. “He couldn’t help himself, could he?” Harbaugh said with a smirk. “He couldn’t help himself.” Skattebo had previously told The New York Post’s Ryan Dunleavy that he was finished with backflips after seeing Hutchinson’s injury. “I’m saying yeah (no more) backflips,” Skattebo said . “Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” However, Dunleavy noted that Skattebo had left open the possibility of bringing the celebration back for a major occasion, such as the playoffs. The victory was another important moment for a Giants team that improved to 6-3-1 and remained top of the NFC East. New York built a 20-6 half-time lead before holding off Jacksonville’s fourth-quarter comeback, with its defence recording three sacks and two interceptions. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
